subject: Error when running the gm.prcomp example

messages.author: 184f7139602fec48
messages.subject: Error when running the gm.prcomp example
parts:
Hello everyone,

I just installed R two month ago and I'm relying a lot on the examples uploaded with the packages. I am currently trying to plot a phylomorphospace analysis using gm.prcomp . But when I tried running the example that is comming with the geomorph package, I got an error returned.


Here is the code I used (which are the 15 first line in the example + library) :

library(geomorph)
data(plethspecies)
Y.gpa <- gpagen(plethspecies$land)    #GPA-alignment

###  Traditional PCA
PCA <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords)
summary(PCA)
plot(PCA, main = "PCA")
plot(PCA, main = "PCA", flip = 1) # flip the first axis
plot(PCA, main = "PCA", axis1 = 3, axis2 = 4) # change PCs viewed

### Phylomorphospace - PCA with phylogeny (result is same as above,
### but with estimated ancestral states projected into plot)
PCA.w.phylo <- gm.prcomp(Y.gpa$coords, phy = plethspecies$phy)
summary(PCA.w.phylo)
plot(PCA.w.phylo, phylo = TRUE, main = "PCA.w.phylo")


And here is the error message (the Tradicional PCA part works just fine) :

> plot(PCA.w.phylo, phylo = TRUE, main = "PCA.w.phylo") Erreur : Some of the arguments in phylo.pars are different than those that are possible (see Arguments).


But it still plotted a graph, just without the phylogeny on it (attached in copy).

Is it a problem in my code that can be solved ? because i didn't touch the data so i dont really see why it would have different arguments than those that are possible...

Thank you for your time !
Célian.

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error when running the gm.prcomp example
parts:
Hi all,

I just updated to the newest version of geomorph and I also replicated this situation with 
plot(PCA.w.phylo, phylo = T, main = "PCA.w.phylo")
.

However, the code seems to run fine if you specify a blank list for phylo.par. 
plot(PCA.w.phylo, phylo = T, main = "PCA.w.phylo", phylo.par = list())

Hope that is helpful!

Bryan
